introduction.heading: What is React?
introduction.description: React is a JavaScript library for building user interfaces out of components - small, reusable functions that each return a description of what should appear on screen. Instead of manually updating the DOM as data changes, you describe the UI for a given piece of state and React figures out the minimal set of DOM changes needed to match it. That one idea - UI as a function of state - is what makes React components predictable and easy to compose into larger apps.

concepts.title: Components
concepts.description: Independent, reusable pieces of UI written as plain JavaScript functions - a component takes props in and returns JSX describing what should appear on screen

concepts.title: JSX
concepts.description: A syntax extension that lets you write HTML-like markup directly in JavaScript; it compiles down to plain function calls that build a tree of elements, and any {expression} inside it is real JavaScript

concepts.title: Props
concepts.description: Data passed from a parent component to a child, always read-only from the child's side - a component can't change its own props, only ask its parent to pass different ones

concepts.title: State
concepts.description: Data a component owns and can update itself with useState; changing it schedules a re-render so the UI stays in sync with the latest value

concepts.title: Hooks
concepts.description: Functions starting with use that let function components tap into state, side effects, and other React features - called at a component's top level, in the same order, on every render

concepts.title: Rendering Lists & Conditionals
concepts.description: Turn an array into elements with .map() and a stable key prop per item, and show or hide UI with &&, ternaries, or an early return - both are just JavaScript, not special syntax

hooks.heading: React Hooks
hooks.description: Hooks are how function components get state, side effects, and other capabilities that used to require class components. useState holds a value across renders and re-renders the component when it changes. useEffect runs code after React commits a render to the screen, and only re-runs when something in its dependency array actually changed; a function returned from an effect is its cleanup, which runs before the next effect and when the component unmounts. Hooks can only be called at a component's top level - never inside a condition, loop, or nested function - so React can match up the same hooks in the same order on every render.

gettingStarted.heading: Getting Started
steps: Create a component as a function that returns JSX - give both the file and the function a capitalized name so React can tell it apart from a plain HTML tag
Add local, changing data with useState(initialValue), and always call its setter instead of reassigning the variable directly
Pass data down to children as props, and pass a function down as a prop when a child needs to notify its parent that something happened
Reach for useEffect only to sync with something outside React - the DOM, a timer, a subscription - and return a cleanup function whenever the effect sets one of those up
Render lists with array.map(), giving each item a stable key prop drawn from your data - never the array index if the list can be reordered or filtered
Reach for React.memo, useMemo, or useCallback only after you've noticed an actual performance problem, not by default

fullExample.heading: Full Example, Step by Step
fullExample.title: A small React app: state, props, and an effect
fullExample.description: This example ties together the core concepts above in one realistic component. Click through the steps to see which lines each one is talking about.
code: // A small presentational component - it only reads the "name" prop,
// useState gives this component its own piece of memory that
// useEffect runs after React commits this render to the screen.
// Because count is in the dependency array, it only re-runs

steps.label: Import the hooks you need
steps.explanation: useState and useEffect are named exports from the "react" package. You only import the hooks a file actually uses.

steps.label: Build a presentational component
steps.explanation: Greeting is just a function that returns JSX. It receives name as a prop and renders it - it has no state of its own, so the same input always produces the same output.

steps.label: Create state with useState
steps.explanation: useState(initialValue) returns a [value, setter] pair. Calling the setter (setName, setCount) tells React this component's data changed and schedules a re-render with the new value.

steps.label: Run side effects with useEffect
steps.explanation: The function passed to useEffect runs after React updates the screen. The dependency array [count] tells React to only re-run it when count changes, instead of after every render.

steps.label: Pass data down as props
steps.explanation: The input's value and onChange are wired to the name state, and that same name is passed into <Greeting name={name} /> as a prop - data flows down from parent to child.

steps.label: Handle events and update state
steps.explanation: onClick is a plain event handler. Calling setCount(count + 1) updates state, which makes App - and anything reading count - re-render with the new value.

steps.label: Export the component
steps.explanation: export default makes App importable from other files, e.g. by the file that mounts it into the page with ReactDOM.createRoot(...).render(<App />).
